financials_interim.notes: COMPANY (standalone parent) basis, same filing/period as GROUP row -- see GROUP row's notes for shared context (segment verification, discontinued-operations base effect, borrowings-field scope). Company Revenue was Rs.33,196k (2026) vs Rs.23,602k (2025), +40.7% YoY, an immaterial trading revenue figure -- BIL's standalone Company result is fundamentally a holding-company structure, not an operating business: Company Total Assets of Rs.316,004,655k are 73.0% Investments in subsidiaries (Rs.230,587,553k, up from Rs.221,107,670k at 31 March 2026). Company Other income/(Expenses) FELL 81.5% YoY to Rs.266,817k (2025: Rs.1,438,006k) -- this single swing is the primary driver of Company Results from operating activities falling 87.3% to Rs.174,250k (2025: Rs.1,375,378k); the nature of the much larger prior-year Other Income figure is not itemised further in this filing (a genuine disclosure gap, not resolved here). Despite the weaker operating result, Company PBT loss NARROWED 18.1% YoY to Rs.(4,909,529)k (2025: Rs.(5,995,814)k), because the Share of Loss of Equity Accounted Investees -- a large standalone-level line reflecting BIL's equity-method accounting for its subsidiaries/associates in the Company's own books (an LKAS 27 policy option, the same pattern seen at BRWN) -- improved by Rs.1,885,075k, from Rs.(4,686,322)k to Rs.(2,801,247)k (40.2% smaller loss); Net Finance Cost also improved 15.0% to Rs.(2,282,532)k (2025: Rs.(2,684,870)k) as Finance income grew 22.0% to Rs.2,945,908k, outpacing a 2.5% rise in Finance cost. No tax expense either period at Company level. Company PAT of Rs.(4,909,529)k ties EXACTLY to the Group's 'Equity holders of the Company' loss attribution for continuing operations -- not a coincidence, a genuine accounting-policy feature of this filing (equity-method Company books). shares_in_issue = 14,369,717,000, same register as Group. EPS cross-check: -4,909,529 / 14,369,717 = -0.3417, ties disclosed -0.34 exactly. Identity check: total_liabilities (7,012 non-current + 132,469,557 current = 132,476,569) + total_equity (183,528,086) = 316,004,655, ties printed Total Assets 316,004,655k exactly. short_term_borrowings = Interest bearing loans and borrowings-current (1,000,000) + Other short term borrowings (9,543,475) + Bank overdrafts (26,983) = 10,570,458k; long_term_borrowings = Interest bearing loans and borrowings (non-current) = nil (dash printed in filing, stored as 0). trade_receivables=40,684,852k (Trade and other receivables) EXCLUDES 'Amounts due from related parties' (Rs.31,827,928k) and 'Loans to related parties' (Rs.6,557,798k), both very large intercompany balances kept separate per line-item discipline. trade_payables=73,781,251k (Trade and other payable) similarly EXCLUDES 'Amounts due to related parties' (Rs.48,090,526k).

Browns Investments PLC (BIL), a LOLC/Browns Group-affiliated diversified conglomerate. GROUP (consolidated) basis. Q1 FY2026/27 ('Quarter ended 30th June 2026') vs Q1 FY2025/26 (quarter ended 30 June 2025) comparative, both explicitly labelled on the face Statement of Profit or Loss (page 4). SEGMENT NOTE (Note 10, Discontinued Operations and Operating Segments, page 10): 5 reportable segments -- Investments, Leisure & Travel, Construction/Manufacturing & trading, Plantation, Real estate -- plus an Adjustments (inter-segment elimination) column and Group Total. Column mapping independently verified: segment Revenue sums exactly to the printed Group Total (33,196+2,993,217+6,450,027+18,952,989+139,451-33,786=28,535,094, ties exactly) and segment PBT sums exactly to Group Total ((4,276,792)+(912,860)+356,420+(472,999)+(50,899)+32,483=(5,324,647), ties exactly) -- both cross-checks passed, so segment figures below are used with confidence. DISCONTINUED OPERATIONS (Note 9, page 10): Browns Ari Resorts (Pvt) Ltd, a Group subsidiary, sold the assets and business of Barcelo Whale Lagoon Maldives Resort for USD 57,500,000 on 19 December 2025 (i.e. within the prior comparative FY, not this quarter); per SLFRS 5 the results of BOTH the current and prior comparative quarter relating to this disposal are presented separately as discontinued operations -- the prior-year comparative quarter (Q1 FY2025/26) therefore carries a Rs.(482,871)k discontinued-operations loss [equity holders Rs.(467,033)k + NCI Rs.(15,838)k] that has NO equivalent in the current quarter (nil), a genuine base effect inflating headline TOTAL-PAT YoY improvement versus the CONTINUING-operations-only comparison -- both are cited and distinguished throughout these notes so they are not conflated. operating_profit = printed face-P&L subtotal 'Results from operating activities' (continuing operations): Rs.4,617,323k (2026) / Rs.2,291,529k (2025), i.e. before Net Finance Cost, Results on acquisition of investments, and Share of profit of equity accounted investees. REVENUE DRIVER: Group continuing-operations Revenue/Income +45% YoY to Rs.28,535,094k (2025: Rs.19,670,957k, +Rs.8,864,137k). Segment attribution: Plantation (largest segment, 66.4% of Group revenue) grew 48.8% to Rs.18,952,989k (2025: Rs.12,735,646k), contributing Rs.6,217,343k -- ~70.1% of the ENTIRE revenue increase on its own; Construction/Manufacturing & trading grew 43.3% to Rs.6,450,027k (2025: Rs.4,500,924k), contributing Rs.1,949,103k (~22.0% of the increase); Leisure & Travel grew 29.1% to Rs.2,993,217k (2025: Rs.2,319,417k), contributing Rs.673,800k (~7.6%); Investments segment revenue (negligible, essentially a treasury/holding segment) grew 40.7% off a tiny base, to Rs.33,196k (2025: Rs.23,602k); Real Estate grew 21.3% to Rs.139,451k. Group Gross Profit more than doubled (+129.2% to Rs.7,171,985k, 2025: Rs.3,128,924k) as Cost of Sales grew only 29% -- Group gross margin expanded from 15.9% to 25.1%, concentrated in the Plantation segment (gross profit +375.3% to Rs.3,374,863k, 2025: Rs.710,028k) and Leisure & Travel (gross profit +44.6% to Rs.2,174,039k, 2025: Rs.1,503,128k). PROFIT DRIVER: despite Results from operating activities more than doubling (+101.5% to Rs.4,617,323k), Group PBT (continuing operations) remained deeply negative at Rs.(5,324,647)k, though this is a Rs.974,044k NARROWING versus the Rs.(6,298,691)k loss in 2025 (loss narrowed ~15.5%), because Net Finance Cost of Rs.(9,970,236)k (2025: Rs.(9,017,700)k, +10.6% YoY) exceeds the entire operating profit by more than double. At the SEGMENT level, two segments swung from an operating LOSS to an operating PROFIT: Leisure & Travel's Results from Operating Activities swung from Rs.(128,796)k (2025) to Rs.2,089,410k (2026), a Rs.2,218,206k improvement, on the back of a large jump in segment Other Income to Rs.2,708,234k (2025: Rs.88,747k) -- BUT segment Net Finance Cost also grew to Rs.(3,002,270)k (2025: Rs.(1,849,372)k, +62.4%), so segment PBT loss only narrowed from Rs.(1,978,167)k to Rs.(912,860)k (53.9% narrower), not a full pass-through of the operating swing; Construction/Manufacturing & trading swung from an operating LOSS of Rs.(435,314)k to an operating PROFIT of Rs.885,713k, and this segment's PBT also swung fully into profit, from Rs.(939,681)k loss to Rs.356,420k profit -- a genuine, full operational turnaround. By contrast, the Investments segment (the Group's treasury/holding-company segment, carrying most of the Group's finance-cost base at Rs.(4,751,848)k Net Finance Cost this quarter) saw its PBT loss WIDEN 38.7% YoY, from Rs.(3,083,099)k to Rs.(4,276,792)k -- now the single largest segment loss and the dominant continuing drag on the Group result, more than offsetting the Leisure & Travel and Construction/Manufacturing improvements combined. Plantation segment PBT loss also widened, from Rs.(230,241)k to Rs.(472,999)k (+105.4% worse), despite the strong revenue and gross-profit growth described above, because segment Net Finance Cost rose 32.3% to Rs.(1,558,370)k (2025: Rs.(1,177,886)k) and Operating Expenses rose 78.2% to Rs.(4,363,094)k (2025: Rs.(2,448,320)k). Income Tax Expense rose to Rs.548,310k from Rs.269,451k (+103.5% YoY) despite the Group-level pretax loss, consistent with segment-level taxable profits emerging in Construction/Manufacturing & trading (tax expense +Rs.200,208k YoY, from Rs.30,767k to Rs.230,975k, tracking that segment's swing into profit) even as other loss-making segments generate no offsetting tax credit at Group level. OTHER COMPREHENSIVE INCOME: Exchange gain from translation of foreign operations was Rs.15,223,611k this quarter, up from Rs.4,244,879k in 2025 (>100% increase) -- consistent with BIL's overseas plantation/leisure exposure (Note 5 discloses translation rates for CNY, EUR, FJD, KES, MUR, RWF, GBP, TZS, AED, USD) -- this swung Total comprehensive income for the period to a POSITIVE Rs.9,403,583k (2025: Rs.(2,800,392)k negative), a much larger and more favourable-looking swing than the underlying trading loss narrowing alone would suggest; flagged so OCI/translation gains are not conflated with operating performance. BALANCE SHEET: total_liabilities = Non-Current (107,316,532) + Current (344,549,688) = 451,866,220k, ties EXACTLY to the segment note's own printed Group Total Liabilities (451,866,220k, Note 10). Identity check: total_liabilities (451,866,220) + total_equity (264,930,512) = 716,796,732, ties printed Total Assets 716,796,732k exactly. short_term_borrowings = Interest bearing loans and borrowings-current (14,583,555) + Other short term borrowings (26,424,957) + Bank overdrafts (20,134,147) = 61,142,659k -- DELIBERATELY EXCLUDES Loans from Related Parties (current, Rs.5,936,561k) and Amounts due to Related Parties (Rs.97,161,332k), both material related-party balances kept separate per line-item discipline (see gaps_note -- the latter alone is larger than total conventional short-term borrowings). long_term_borrowings = Interest bearing loans and borrowings (non-current) only (26,179,310k), excludes Lease Liability (13,765,117) and non-current Loans from Related Parties (755,503). trade_payables = 'Trade and other payable' (178,126,558k) as printed, a combined line, excluding Amounts due to related parties. depreciation_amortization = Depreciation/amortization recognised to cost of sales (1,294,224) + recognised to Administration and distribution costs (1,094,459) = 2,388,683k, per the Cash Flow Statement (page 7) -- NOTE the face Income Statement only shows the Rs.1,094,459k opex-portion as a separate line item BELOW Gross Profit; the Rs.1,294,224k cost-of-sales-embedded portion is not separately visible on the face P&L, only in the cash flow reconciliation -- flagged so the two are not confused. cash_and_equivalents=4,916,726k is the face BS 'Cash and cash equivalents'; the Cash Flow Statement's 'Cash and cash equivalents at end of period' is NEGATIVE Rs.(15,217,421)k because its own Note A explicitly nets Bank overdrafts (Rs.20,134,147k) against cash (Rs.4,916,726k) -- an EXPLICITLY RECONCILED definitional difference disclosed by the filing itself, not an unresolved gap. shares_in_issue = 14,369,717,000 (Note 3, 'Ordinary Shares Nos.000' = 14,369,717 thousand shares). EPS cross-check: -4,909,529 (equity-holders' share of continuing+total PAT, identical this quarter since discontinued=nil) / 14,369,717 (thousand shares) = -0.3417, ties disclosed -0.34 exactly. profit_after_tax is stored as the Group TOTAL 'Profit/(loss) for the period' (-5,872,957k, ties the PBT-tax_expense=PAT soft validation check on a CONTINUING-operations basis since this quarter has zero discontinued-operations result); minority_interest=(963,428)k is NCI's share, stored separately; eps_basic=(0.34) is based on the PARENT-ONLY (equity holders of the Company) loss of (4,909,529)k, a DIFFERENT number from the Group-total profit_after_tax figure -- flagged explicitly here per this database's established convention (see SHL, BRWN entries for the same pattern).

interim_updates.note_text: Browns Investments PLC (BIL) narrowed its Group net loss from continuing operations 10.6% YoY to Rs.5,872.96mn for Q1 FY2026/27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026), from Rs.6,568.14mn a year earlier, on Group continuing-operations revenue up 45% YoY to Rs.28,535.09mn (2025: Rs.19,670.96mn). Including the prior-year quarter's Rs.482.87mn discontinued-operations loss (from Browns Ari Resorts' sale of the Barcelo Whale Lagoon Maldives Resort for USD 57.5mn, completed December 2025 -- nil equivalent this quarter), the TOTAL Group net loss narrowed by a larger 16.7%, to Rs.5,872.96mn from Rs.7,051.01mn; the extra ~6 percentage points of improvement in the total-basis comparison is a base effect from the now-divested resort, not a trading improvement, so continuing-operations figures are used as the primary comparison here. By segment (Note 10, cross-checked: segment revenue sums to Group Total Rs.28,535,094k and segment PBT to Rs.(5,324,647)k, both exact): Plantation (66.4% of Group revenue, the largest segment) drove the great majority of the revenue increase -- revenue +48.8% YoY to Rs.18,952.99mn (2025: Rs.12,735.65mn), contributing Rs.6,217.34mn of the Group's Rs.8,864.14mn revenue increase (~70.1% on its own) -- but Plantation segment PBT loss WIDENED 105.4% to Rs.(472.999)mn (2025: Rs.(230.241)mn) despite the strong top-line growth, because segment Operating Expenses rose 78.2% to Rs.4,363.094mn and segment Net Finance Cost rose 32.3% to Rs.1,558.37mn. Two segments swung from an operating LOSS to an operating PROFIT: Construction/Manufacturing & trading swung fully into profit at both the operating AND PBT line -- Results from Operating Activities from Rs.(435.31)mn loss to Rs.885.71mn profit, PBT from Rs.(939.68)mn loss to Rs.356.42mn profit, a genuine Rs.1,296.10mn PBT turnaround -- while Leisure & Travel's operating result swung from Rs.(128.80)mn loss to Rs.2,089.41mn profit (largely on a jump in segment Other Income to Rs.2,708.23mn from Rs.88.75mn) but its PBT improvement was smaller (loss narrowed from Rs.(1,978.17)mn to Rs.(912.86)mn, 53.9% narrower) because segment Net Finance Cost also grew 62.4% to Rs.3,002.27mn -- a finance-cost drag similar to the pattern seen in BRWN's Leisure & Property segment this quarter. Working against these improvements, the Investments segment -- the Group's treasury/holding-company segment, carrying the largest share of Group Net Finance Cost at Rs.4,751.85mn this quarter -- saw its PBT loss WIDEN 38.7% YoY, from Rs.(3,083.10)mn to Rs.(4,276.79)mn, now the single largest segment loss and the dominant continuing drag on the Group result, exceeding the combined improvement from Construction/ Manufacturing and Leisure & Travel. At Group level, Results from operating activities more than doubled (+101.5% to Rs.4,617.32mn), but Net Finance Cost of Rs.9,970.24mn (+10.6% YoY) still exceeds the entire operating profit by more than double, which is why the 15.5% narrowing in Group PBT loss (to Rs.(5,324.65)mn) lagged well behind the operating-profit improvement. Income Tax Expense rose 103.5% YoY to Rs.548.31mn (2025: Rs.269.45mn) despite the Group pretax loss, tracking the Construction/Manufacturing & trading segment's swing into taxable profit (segment tax expense +Rs.200.21mn YoY). Basic/diluted loss per share from continuing operations improved to Rs.(0.34) from Rs.(0.42) a year earlier. A large Exchange gain from translation of foreign operations (Rs.15,223.61mn this quarter vs Rs.4,244.88mn PY) drove Total comprehensive income for the period to a positive Rs.9,403.58mn (2025: Rs.(2,800.39)mn negative) -- a much more favourable-looking swing than the underlying trading-loss narrowing alone, and should not be read as an operating improvement. At standalone COMPANY (parent-only, holding-company) level, Other income collapsed 81.5% YoY to Rs.266.82mn (2025: Rs.1,438.01mn), the primary driver of an 87.3% fall in Company operating profit to Rs.174.25mn (2025: Rs.1,375.38mn); despite this, Company PBT loss still narrowed 18.1% to Rs.(4,909.53)mn (2025: Rs.(5,995.81)mn) because the Share of Loss of Equity Accounted Investees (BIL's equity-method accounting for its subsidiaries at standalone level) improved 40.2%, from Rs.(4,686.32)mn to Rs.(2,801.25)mn.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: this is the first financial_statements/interim_updates entry for BIL in this database, no prior quarter collected. profit_before_tax/tax_expense/profit_after_tax as stored are on a CONTINUING-OPERATIONS basis (they coincide exactly with TOTAL-basis figures for the current quarter, since discontinued operations = nil this period, but the PY comparative differs: continuing-only PAT was Rs.(6,568,142)k vs TOTAL PAT of Rs.(7,051,013)k, a Rs.482,871k gap from the Barcelo Whale Lagoon Maldives Resort discontinued-operations loss) -- both bases are cited in note_text so the YoY improvement is not overstated by conflating a base effect (resort divestment) with genuine operating improvement. profit_after_tax is stored as the Group TOTAL 'Profit/(loss) for the period' (continuing-operations basis, -5,872,957, ties the PBT-tax_expense=PAT soft validation check); this is DIFFERENT from the Rs.(4,909,529)k loss attributable to equity holders of the Company, which is what eps_basic (-0.34) is actually based on -- both figures are cited and reconciled above, flagged again here so the two are not conflated (same pattern as the SHL and BRWN entries in this database). The Investments segment's Rs.4,751,848k Net Finance Cost and Rs.745,597k Other Income are not broken down by underlying instrument/investee in this filing, so the exact composition of the 38.7% PBT deterioration in that segment cannot be decomposed further than the segment-level figures cited. short_term_borrowings and long_term_borrowings as mapped deliberately EXCLUDE two very large related-party funding lines -- 'Amounts due to related parties' (Rs.97,161,332k, larger than total conventional short-term borrowings) and 'Loans from related parties' (current, Rs.5,936,561k) -- kept separate per line-item discipline; the filing gives no further detail on the nature/terms of these related-party balances, a genuine disclosure gap worth flagging given their size relative to the Group's Rs.264,930,512k total equity. The nature of the Rs.1,438,006k prior-year Company-level Other Income figure (vs only Rs.266,817k this quarter, an 81.5% fall) is not itemised in the filing -- a genuine disclosure gap, not resolved by this entry. capex is mapped to the single combined cash-flow line 'Acquisition and construction of property, plant and equipment' (Rs.4,929,552k Group / Rs.331k Company), which excludes separately-disclosed cash flows for biological-asset investment (Rs.528,687k) and other financial assets (Rs.97,932k) at Group level -- kept separate per line-item discipline, cited here for completeness.
interim_updates.takeaway: BIL's Group net loss from continuing operations narrowed 10.6% YoY on strong 45% revenue growth concentrated in the Plantation segment (+48.8%, ~70.1% of the total revenue increase) and a genuine operational turnaround in Construction/Manufacturing & trading (a Rs.1,296.10mn PBT swing from loss to profit), but the improvement was capped by the Investments segment's PBT loss widening 38.7% to Rs.(4,276.79)mn -- the Group's treasury/holding segment, which carries the bulk of finance costs and is now the single largest segment loss, exceeding the combined improvement from the two turnaround segments. Group Net Finance Cost (Rs.9,970.24mn, +10.6% YoY) still exceeds the entire operating profit by more than double, so despite Results from operating activities more than doubling, the PBT loss only narrowed 15.5% -- leverage, not trading, remains the binding constraint, echoing the same pattern seen at BRWN this quarter. The reported 16.7% TOTAL-basis loss narrowing partly reflects the absence of a Rs.482.87mn discontinued-operations loss from the now-divested Barcelo Whale Lagoon Maldives Resort in the prior-year comparative, a base effect that should not be read as incremental trading improvement. A large Rs.15,223.61mn foreign-currency translation gain (vs Rs.4,244.88mn PY) drove Total comprehensive income sharply positive, Rs.9,403.58mn vs a negative Rs.(2,800.39)mn a year earlier, but this is an OCI/FX item, not an operating one, and should be read separately from the trading result.

operational_highlights: Group continuing-operations Revenue Rs.28,535.09mn, +45% YoY (2025: Rs.19,670.96mn); Group net loss (continuing) narrowed 10.6% YoY to Rs.5,872.96mn (2025: Rs.6,568.14mn); on a TOTAL basis (incl. the now-divested Maldives resort) the loss narrowed a larger 16.7%, a base effect not a trading improvement.

Plantation segment (66.4% of Group revenue) contributed ~70.1% of the entire Group revenue increase: revenue +48.8% YoY to Rs.18,952.99mn, but segment PBT loss WIDENED 105.4% to Rs.(472.999)mn as segment Operating Expenses rose 78.2% and Net Finance Cost rose 32.3%.
Construction/Manufacturing & trading swung fully into profit YoY: Results from Operating Activities from Rs.(435.31)mn loss to Rs.885.71mn profit; PBT from Rs.(939.68)mn loss to Rs.356.42mn profit.

Leisure & Travel operating result swung from Rs.(128.80)mn loss to Rs.2,089.41mn profit, but PBT improvement was smaller (loss narrowed only to Rs.(912.86)mn from Rs.(1,978.17)mn) as segment Net Finance Cost grew 62.4% to Rs.3,002.27mn.

Investments segment (Group treasury/holding segment) PBT loss WIDENED 38.7% YoY to Rs.(4,276.79)mn -- now the largest single segment loss, exceeding the combined PBT improvement from Construction/Manufacturing and Leisure & Travel.
Group Net Finance Cost Rs.9,970.24mn (+10.6% YoY) still exceeds the more-than-doubled Rs.4,617.32mn operating profit, capping the Group PBT loss narrowing to 15.5% despite the operating surge.

Exchange gain from translation of foreign operations Rs.15,223.61mn (vs Rs.4,244.88mn PY) drove Total comprehensive income to a positive Rs.9,403.58mn (2025: Rs.(2,800.39)mn negative) -- an OCI/FX-driven swing, not an operating one.

Company (standalone) Other income fell 81.5% YoY to Rs.266.82mn, driving an 87.3% fall in Company operating profit to Rs.174.25mn, though Company PBT loss still narrowed 18.1% on a 40.2% improvement in Share of Loss of Equity Accounted Investees.
key_drivers: Plantation segment revenue growth (+48.8% YoY to Rs.18,952.99mn) contributed ~70.1% of the Group's entire Rs.8,864.14mn revenue increase, the single largest driver of top-line growth, even as the segment's own PBT loss widened on higher opex and finance costs.

Investments segment (treasury/holding) PBT loss widening 38.7% YoY to Rs.(4,276.79)mn is the dominant negative driver at Group level, outweighing genuine operational turnarounds in Construction/Manufacturing (+Rs.1,296.10mn PBT swing) and the operating (but not PBT) improvement in Leisure & Travel.
Group Net Finance Cost of Rs.9,970.24mn (+10.6% YoY) exceeding the Rs.4,617.32mn operating profit by more than double is why a 101.5% operating-profit surge only narrowed the Group PBT loss by 15.5%.

The prior-year quarter's Rs.482.87mn discontinued-operations loss (Barcelo Whale Lagoon Maldives Resort, divested December 2025) does not recur this quarter, inflating the TOTAL-basis YoY loss narrowing (16.7%) relative to the CONTINUING-operations-only comparison (10.6%) -- a base effect, not a trading improvement.
